items.q: What makes Clever Way Media different?
items.a: We combine classic marketing with AI automation. Smart systems take over repetitive tasks — from lead generation and AI chatbots to receipt processing — connected to the tools you already use. You save time and win new customers predictably.

items.q: Do you also build custom software for businesses?
items.a: Yes. Alongside websites and marketing, we build personalized programs that make running your company much easier — for example customer and order management, appointment scheduling, quote and invoicing tools, or dashboards with your key numbers. Everything tailored exactly to how you work and connected to the tools you already use.

items.q: Which AI automations do you offer?
items.a: Among others: an AI phone assistant that answers calls around the clock and books appointments; automated lead generation; AI chatbots for your website and WhatsApp; lead qualification with CRM integration; invoice and receipt processing (DATEV, lexoffice, sevDesk); quote and document generators; content and reporting automation; and custom workflow automations that seamlessly connect your tools.

items.q: How much does a website or ongoing support cost?
items.a: The Starter Package starts at a one-time €799. For ongoing marketing and automation there are monthly packages from €530, as well as custom packages. In the free strategy call we'll find the right model for you.

items.q: Which languages and regions do you work in?
items.a: We work with businesses in Germany, Hungary and Romania — always in the local language. Website, communication and support are available in German, Hungarian and Romanian, and in English on request.

items.q: How quickly will I see results?
items.a: Websites and campaigns often go live within a few weeks. Paid ads and AI automations bring first contacts quickly, while SEO unfolds its full effect in the medium term.

ki-telefonassistent.title: Never lose a call again
ki-telefonassistent.challenge: Note: an illustrative example, not a real client case. Many small businesses can't answer the phone while they're working — and every missed call is a potentially lost job, because callers often go straight to the next provider.
ki-telefonassistent.strategy: An AI phone assistant takes the calls that would otherwise go unanswered: it answers on behalf of the business, records name, number and request, books an appointment straight into the calendar if needed, and forwards urgent cases immediately. At the start of the call it transparently discloses that it's a digital assistant — GDPR-compliant.
executionSteps: Setting up conditional call forwarding (when busy, unanswered or outside business hours)
A custom call script in the business's tone, including a GDPR notice
Calendar integration for automatic appointment booking
Instant notification via SMS, email or WhatsApp after every call

website-kosten-2026.title: Website Costs in 2026: What Does a Professional Website Really Cost?
website-kosten-2026.seoTitle: Website Costs 2026: What Does a Website Really Cost?
website-kosten-2026.description: Realistic price ranges for business websites in 2026 — from a simple presence site to a complete package with automation. No hidden costs.
website-kosten-2026.excerpt: The honest answer to the question almost everyone asks before hiring an agency — including the factors that really drive the price.

body.text: The question "How much does a website cost?" can't be answered with a single number — any more than "How much does a car cost?". Still, there are realistic ranges you can use as a guide before talking to agencies.
The three main factors that determine the price

items: Scope: a 3-page presence site costs much less than an online shop with hundreds of products.
Individuality: a website-builder template is cheaper than a fully custom design.
Extra features: appointment booking, multilingual content or automation increase the effort.

body.text: Realistic price ranges

For a simple, professional website with 1–5 pages, reputable quotes usually range from €700 to €1,500 one-time. For an online shop or a website with ongoing support (SEO, content, ads), monthly models between €250 and €900 are common, often combined with a one-time setup fee.
Much cheaper offers are usually templates without any real adaptation to your business. Much more expensive offers often only pay off for very large companies with complex requirements.
What to look out for
Ask specifically: is basic SEO included? Who maintains the content later? What happens after the project ends? A reputable quote answers these questions without dodging them.

At Clever Way Media, website projects start at a one-time €799 for the Starter Package — transparently itemized, with no hidden extra costs. For ongoing marketing and automation there are monthly packages from €530.

faq.q: Is a cheap website a bad website?
faq.a: Not necessarily — but very cheap offers are often unmodified templates with no real strategy behind them.

faq.q: Is paying monthly better than a one-time payment?
faq.a: If ongoing support (SEO, content, ads) is included, yes — then you're paying for continuous work, not just the one-time build.

steuerkanzlei-mandanten-gewinnen.title: Winning Clients as a Tax Firm: 5 Approaches That Really Work in 2026
steuerkanzlei-mandanten-gewinnen.seoTitle: Tax Firms: 5 Ways to Win New Clients in 2026
steuerkanzlei-mandanten-gewinnen.description: How tax firms can win new clients predictably — without relying on chance referrals. With concrete, actionable approaches.
steuerkanzlei-mandanten-gewinnen.excerpt: Referrals alone rarely drive growth. These five approaches bring in new inquiries predictably — even without extra sales staff.

body.text: Most tax firms grow through referrals — a model that has worked for a long time but is hard to scale. If you want to grow actively, you need additional, predictable channels.
1. A website that builds trust before the first call

Many firm websites are outdated or purely informational. A modern website with a clear specialization (e.g. in certain industries or company sizes) helps potential clients decide on you before they even get in touch.
2. Targeted, automated outreach instead of manual cold calling
Manual cold outreach is time-consuming and scales poorly. An AI-powered email system can reach out specifically to companies that match your ideal client profile — personalized, yet automated.
3. Use LinkedIn as a professional channel
Regular, expert content on LinkedIn positions you as a specialist — an underrated channel, especially for B2B clients.
4. Local SEO for regional visibility
Anyone searching Google for "tax advisor [city]" should find you — not just the biggest firm in town. An optimized Google Business Profile is the foundation for that.
5. Automatic prospect follow-up
A prospect who doesn't reply right away isn't lost — as long as they're followed up. Automated follow-ups that still feel personal noticeably increase your success rate.
Together, these five building blocks form a complete client-acquisition system at Clever Way Media — implemented as a whole or one piece at a time.

faq.q: Is automated cold email outreach GDPR-compliant?
faq.a: Yes, if the campaigns are set up within the applicable rules for B2B outreach.

faq.q: How quickly do first results show?
faq.a: Additional inquiries often appear within 4–6 weeks of setup.

seo-oder-google-ads.title: SEO or Google Ads: Which Pays Off More for Small Businesses?
seo-oder-google-ads.description: An honest comparison of SEO and Google Ads for small and medium-sized businesses — costs, time horizon and when each channel makes sense.
seo-oder-google-ads.excerpt: The most common marketing question small businesses ask — and why the answer is usually "both, but at different times".

body.text: There's no one-size-fits-all answer — but there are clear criteria that help you decide.
Google Ads: fast, but you pay continuously
Google Ads delivers visibility from day one. As soon as the budget pauses, the visibility disappears too. Ideal for quick results, product launches or seasonal offers.
SEO: slow start, but a lasting effect
SEO takes time — often 3 to 6 months for noticeable effects. In return, the visibility stays even without an ongoing budget and keeps building over time.
A simple rule of thumb

If you need revenue in the short term (e.g. a new business opening, seasonal business), Google Ads is the faster lever. If you want to grow more independently of ad spend in the long run, SEO is the better investment.
In practice the combination works best: Google Ads for immediate results while SEO is built up in the background — so your dependence on paid advertising decreases over time.

faq.q: Can I do both with a small budget?
faq.a: Yes — it often makes sense to start with a smaller ads budget and build the SEO foundations in parallel.

faq.q: How long until SEO can replace Google Ads?
faq.a: That depends heavily on your industry and competition — 6–12 months is realistic before SEO can take over most of your visibility.

ki-automatisierung-einstieg.title: AI Automation for Small Businesses: Where You Should Really Start
ki-automatisierung-einstieg.seoTitle: AI Automation for Small Businesses: Where to Start
ki-automatisierung-einstieg.description: AI automation sounds complex — but it doesn't have to be. These three starting points deliver the biggest effect with manageable effort.
ki-automatisierung-einstieg.excerpt: Not every automation makes equal sense. These three areas bring the fastest, most noticeable benefit for most small businesses.

body.text: "AI automation" often sounds like a big, complicated project — yet a small, targeted start usually pays off far more than a large all-in-one solution from the outset.
1. Automated lead generation
Instead of writing emails by hand, an AI handles personalized outreach to potential customers — in the background, without anyone on your team spending hours on it.
2. Lead qualification and CRM integration
New inquiries are scored and prioritized automatically. Your team no longer wastes time on unsuitable inquiries and handles the most promising contacts first.
3. An AI chatbot for frequent questions
Most incoming questions repeat themselves — opening hours, prices, availability. A chatbot answers them instantly, even outside business hours.
How to find the right starting point
Ask yourself: where does my team currently lose the most time on repetitive tasks? That's exactly where the first automation step pays off most — not where it sounds the most "modern".

faq.q: Do I need technical knowledge for AI automation?
faq.a: No, we handle the setup — you then use a ready-made system.

faq.q: Does it work with my existing tools?
faq.a: Usually yes — practically any common tool with an API can be connected.

local-seo-checkliste.title: Local SEO Checklist: How to Get Found on Google Maps
local-seo-checkliste.description: A practical checklist for restaurants, tradespeople and local service providers to get found more easily on Google Maps and in local search.
local-seo-checkliste.excerpt: Most local businesses only use half of their Google Business Profile's potential. This checklist shows what really makes a difference.

body.text: When someone searches for "restaurant near me" or "hairdresser [neighborhood]", it's often the Google Business Profile that decides who gets the call — not the actual website.
The key points at a glance

items: A complete Google Business Profile with the correct category, address and opening hours
Current, high-quality photos — interior, products, team
Consistent details (name, address, phone number) across all platforms
Actively replying to reviews, positive and negative
Local keywords on your own website (city, neighborhood, region)
Regular posts on your Google Business Profile

body.text: The most underrated point: reviews

The number and recency of reviews influence both your ranking and the searcher's decision. A system for actively asking for reviews and replying to them professionally usually pays off faster than many other measures.

faq.q: How quickly does local SEO have an effect?
faq.a: Often faster than classic SEO — first improvements are frequently visible within a few weeks.

faq.q: Is an optimized Google profile enough on its own?
faq.a: It's the most important foundation, but it works best combined with a locally optimized website.

social-media-kosten.title: How Much Does Social Media Management Cost? A Realistic Price Overview
social-media-kosten.seoTitle: Social Media Management Costs: Realistic Prices
social-media-kosten.description: What professional social media management really costs — and what the price depends on. A realistic overview without marketing fluff.
social-media-kosten.excerpt: Between €0 freelancer offers and five-figure agency retainers there's a huge range. Here are the realistic factors behind it.

body.text: Prices for social media management vary widely — mostly because "management" can be defined in very different ways.
What influences the price

items: Number of posts per week
Number of platforms managed (Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn)
Whether new photo/video material is created or existing material is used
Whether community management (comments, messages) is included
Whether paid advertising runs in addition

body.text: Realistic price ranges

For solid basic management with a few posts per week, reputable monthly prices usually range from €250 to €500. More extensive packages with content production, community management and ad management often range from €500 to €900 per month.
Much cheaper offers usually mean far fewer posts or just planning without real management.

faq.q: Do I need my own photos?
faq.a: It helps, but it's not essential — we also work with existing material and add to it where needed.

faq.q: Is the ad budget included in the management fee?
faq.a: No, you pay the ad budget directly to the platform — the management fee covers the work, not the ad spend.

teaser.h2: How good is your website really?

popup.title: How good is your website really?
popup.text: Find out in seconds what's holding back customers and Google on your site — with concrete tips.
popup.trust: Free · No sign-up · Results in seconds

speed.name: Mobile loading speed
speed.tip: Compress images (WebP), remove unnecessary scripts and plugins, and use fast hosting. Every second of loading time costs you inquiries.

https.name: Secure connection (HTTPS)
https.pass: Your site is served encrypted over HTTPS.
https.fail: Your site isn't encrypted — browsers show a "Not secure" warning.
https.tip: Enable an SSL certificate (free with most hosts) and redirect all traffic to HTTPS.

response.name: Server response time
response.warn: The server responds a bit slowly ({value} ms).
response.fail: The server responds very slowly ({value} ms).
response.tip: Enable caching or switch to faster hosting. Under 800 ms is a good value.

viewport.name: Mobile display
viewport.pass: The site is set up for smartphones.
viewport.fail: The site isn't optimized for smartphones — even though most visitors usually come on mobile.
viewport.tip: Use a responsive layout with a viewport tag so text and buttons are easy to use on a phone.

title.name: Page title for Google
title.pass: The page title is present and a good length ({value} characters).
title.warn: The page title has an unfavorable length ({value} characters) — too short wastes potential, too long gets cut off by Google.
title.fail: The page title is missing — Google doesn't know how to display your page.
title.tip: Write a 15–65 character title: service + location + company name, e.g. "Hair Salon in Manchester | Salon Example".

description.name: Description in search results
description.pass: The meta description is present and well sized ({value} characters).
description.warn: The meta description has an unfavorable length ({value} characters) — too short doesn't convince, too long gets cut off.
description.fail: The meta description is missing — Google then picks a random text snippet.
description.tip: 70–165 characters combining your benefit and a call to action — it's your ad in the search results.

h1.name: Main heading (H1)
h1.pass: Exactly one main heading — cleanly structured.
h1.warn: There are {value} main headings — that dilutes the page's topic.
h1.tip: Exactly one H1 per page that clearly says what you offer and where.

contact.name: Contact options
contact.pass: Visitors can call you with a single tap.
contact.warn: Contact is possible, but a tap-to-call phone number is missing.
contact.fail: There's no direct way to get in touch on the homepage.
contact.tip: Place a tap-to-call phone number, email or WhatsApp where it's easy to see — ideally in the header too.

legal.name: Legal notice & privacy policy
legal.pass: Legal notice and privacy policy are linked.
legal.warn: The legal notice or privacy policy is missing from the homepage.
legal.fail: Neither a legal notice nor a privacy policy is linked — in Germany this can lead to legal warnings.
legal.tip: Link both pages from every page, e.g. in the footer.

schema.name: Structured data for Google
schema.pass: Google receives your business details in a structured format.
schema.warn: There is structured data, but no business details.
schema.fail: No structured data — Google has to guess your business details.
schema.tip: Add LocalBusiness markup with name, address, phone and opening hours. It strengthens local visibility.

alt.name: Image descriptions (alt text)
alt.warn: Only {value}% of images have a description.
alt.fail: Only {value}% of images have a description.
alt.tip: Give every image a short, descriptive alt text — good for Google Images and accessibility.

crawl.name: robots.txt & sitemap
crawl.warn: robots.txt or the sitemap is missing.
crawl.fail: Neither robots.txt nor a sitemap was found.
crawl.tip: Create a sitemap.xml and submit it in Google Search Console so all your pages get found.

og.name: Link preview when shared
og.pass: A nice preview appears when shared on WhatsApp, Facebook and co.
og.fail: No appealing preview appears when the page is shared.
og.tip: Set an Open Graph title and image so shared links look professional.

lang.name: Language tag
lang.pass: The page language is set correctly.
lang.tip: Set the lang attribute (e.g. "en") — it helps Google and screen readers.

favicon.name: Favicon
favicon.warn: The favicon is missing from the browser tab.
favicon.fail: The favicon is missing from the browser tab.
favicon.tip: Add your logo as a small icon — it looks more professional and also shows up in Google.
